outcome: Malicious and impersonation emails are stopped before they reach a mailbox, and the domain is protected against being spoofed.
overview: Most successful intrusions still start with a message somebody was willing to believe, and the messages that work best carry no malware at all — an invoice with changed bank details, a request from a name the recipient recognises. FortiMail inspects mail before it reaches the mailbox, combining attachment and link analysis with sender authentication checks that catch the impersonation cases signature scanning cannot. The part organisations underestimate is authentication: publishing and enforcing sender policy for your own domain is what stops your name being used against your customers, and it is usually the first finding.

benefits.text: Malicious attachments and links are analysed before delivery rather than after a click
benefits.limits: Detection is never complete; the measure that matters is what the user reporting path catches afterwards, which is why it is part of the design

benefits.text: Impersonation of internal senders and known suppliers is detected through authentication and heuristics
benefits.limits: Effective against domain spoofing; a genuinely compromised supplier mailbox is authentic mail and needs process controls on payment changes, not filtering

benefits.text: The organisation’s own domain stops being usable for spoofing once sender policy is enforced
benefits.limits: Enforcement can break legitimate third-party senders that were never inventoried; the reporting period before enforcement exists for exactly that reason

residency: Available as an appliance or virtual machine in the customer estate, so message content and quarantine can stay in-country where a hosted service would not allow it

notFor.situation: An organisation already running an equivalent gateway in front of the same mail platform
notFor.why: Two gateways in the mail path double the false-positive surface and make delivery problems hard to attribute

notFor.situation: A tenant satisfied with its mail platform’s built-in protection and with authentication already enforced
notFor.why: The remaining gap may not justify another hop in the mail path

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Fortinet implementation partner · Duration: 4–8 weeks to a tuned gateway; authentication enforcement follows the reporting period
Support model: Vendor hardware and subscription support; Redington coordinates the vendor case. Optional managed tuning with an agreed release-time target.
1) Assessment — mail flow, current filtering, authentication state and third-party sender inventory
2) Design — routing, policy set, quarantine behaviour, release ownership and the reporting route
3) Deploy and tune — gateway in path, policy tuned against live mail, reporting route live
4) Enforce and hand over — authentication moved to enforcement on the customer’s change, operations handed over
deliverables: A user-reported message reaches the tuning path and results in a recorded policy decision
Quarantine release meets the agreed target time during a normal working week
Aggregate authentication reports show every legitimate sender aligned before enforcement is proposed

languages: English delivery; Arabic user-facing quarantine notifications supported
